content:
maria_support: Customer (Jamie) reports EventSource stream dropping in Safari + some browsers when behind a CDN. They see partial event payloads and then a stalled reconnect loop. Tried polyfill, still flaky.

jamie_customer: Repro: open https://edge.example.com/sse/stream with Safari 16.4 on macOS, login cookie present (SameSite=None; Secure). Connection establishes, a few events arrive, then nothing for ~30-90s. Client eventually reconnects but gets only partial event (truncated JSON). Happens behind our CDN (Fastly) but not when hitting origin directly.

ash_engineer: Can you paste request/response headers from the failing case and a curl that reproduces? Also does the origin keep the connection open and periodically flush? Safari is notorious about buffering small writes.

jamie_customer: Headers (edge -> client):
  GET /sse/stream HTTP/1.1
  Host: edge.example.com
  Accept: text/event-stream
  Cookie: session=XXX; SameSite=None; Secure
  Origin: https://app.example.com

Response (edge cached):
  HTTP/1.1 200 OK
  Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
  Cache-Control: max-age=300
  Vary: Accept-Encoding
  Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.example.com
  Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
  Set-Cookie: session=XXX; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=None
  Transfer-Encoding: chunked

curl repro (fail):
  curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Origin: https://app.example.com" -b "session=XXX" "https://edge.example.com/sse/stream"

Note: when I curl the origin directly (origin.example.internal), stream runs fine for 20+ mins. Only edge seems to insert 304/304-ish caching behavior intermittently and then Safari stalls. When we remove cookie or hit from Chrome it works.

ash_engineer: Important pieces: 1) CDN caching (Cache-Control + Vary) 2) Cookies being present + credentials allowed 3) Safari buffering small chunks until a certain size or connection heuristics 4) 304/edge behavior on conditional requests can close the SSE connection.

ben_infra: @ash_engineer @maria_support quick checklist:
- Ensure SSE responses are never cached by CDN: Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate or Cache-Control: private, no-transform and set Surrogate-Control: no-store at edge.
- Remove Vary: Accept-Encoding on SSE path (or set Vary: *) carefully; Vary prevents consistent cache key and might cause conditional requests -> 304.
- Make sure the CDN forwards Authorization/Cookie as needed and does not serve cached 304 for authenticated SSE.
- Add Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true at origin and ensure CDN preserves it (no wildcard origin with credentials).
- Chunk flush: server should send a keepalive comment every ~15s (":\n") and pad chunks to force TCP flushes.

maria_support: Jamie confirmed edge sometimes returns 304 when origin responds 200 but CDN thinks resource unchanged due to Vary mismatch. Also, Fastly config has a global caching rule that caches any 200 with Cache-Control < 600s.

ash_engineer: Repro idea: run a curl that simulates Safari (small windowing) + check for presence of Content-Length vs Transfer-Encoding. If CDN strips Transfer-Encoding or converts to content-length with an early content-length it will buffer.

jamie_customer: Quick test: origin sends chunked, but Fastly rewrites as content-length for cached objects. When we enable "bypass caching for /sse/*" the problem stops. But that's not a long-term solution; customer needs guides for customers using their CDN and for our platform.

ben_infra: Action items:
- eng-infra to add a recommended CDN policy for SSE endpoints (no-cache, Surrogate-Control: no-store, preserve TE: chunked, pass cookies, do not normalize Content-Length)
- SDK/docs: add Safari polyfill notes and explicit withCredentials guidance (Access-Control-Allow-Credentials + explicit origin header, not '*')
- Support: advise customer to disable caching on SSE routes and add keepalive comments to server output as immediate workaround

ash_engineer: Short-term workaround for customer:
1) Disable CDN caching for /sse/stream routes (Fastly: request condition -> pass) OR set Surrogate-Control: no-store for those responses.
2) Ensure origin sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.example.com (exact origin) and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Do not use '*'.
3) Send initial padding and periodic keepalive comments, e.g. server sends:

  :ok
  :padding -----------------------------------------------------\n\n
then each event uses double-newline end. Also flush after each write.

maria_support: Also note: if using EventSource with credentials in the browser, you must set new EventSource(url, { withCredentials: true }) in polyfills; native EventSource (Chrome) ignores withCredentials in older implementations. Safari required cross-site cookies to be SameSite=None and Secure.

jamie_customer: We tried polyfill (eventsource-polyfill) with withCredentials true; still saw stalls until we turned off CDN caching. Polyfill didn't mitigate CDN rewrite.

ash_engineer: FYI edge-case: some CDNs will cache and serve 206/304 or attempt range requests for SSE if Vary/ETag present. Recommend removing ETag and any conditional cache validators for SSE responses.

ben_infra: Created infra ticket INFRA-7892 to publish recommended Fastly snippet and a redirect rule to bypass edge for /sse/*, assigned to @ben_infra. Link: https://redwood-internal/infra/INFRA-7892

maria_support: I've sent customer a step-by-step: disable caching on SSE routes, confirm Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is preserved, and add keepalive comment every 10s. Customer will test and update.

deploy-bot: Deployment started for edge rule update (fastly-change-#4321) — expecting config to propagate in ~5m.

jamie_customer: after edge rule update and turning off caching for /sse/* it's stable for 40m in Safari. Thanks! Will monitor for next 24h and report.

maria_support: Marking this thread: resolved->waiting-monitor. If problem recurs we'll reopen INFRA-7892 and engage eng-runtime for deeper kernel/flush analysis.

ash_engineer: Notes for docs (small bullets):
- SSE must not be cached by intermediary CDNs
- Preserve TE: chunked and Transfer-Encoding headers
- For cross-site SSE with cookies: set Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true and explicit origin
- Add keepalive comments and pad to force TCP flush (Safari buffers tiny writes)
- Avoid ETag/304 on SSE routes

participants: maria_support, jamie_customer, ash_engineer, ben_infra, deploy-bot
